- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or volatility — adjust downward by 1–2% for 3–5 day lag.
- When sentiment drops below 0.3, model tends to overcorrect — apply a mild upward bias to prevent undershoot.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Overshoot after high sentiment spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment drops sharply within 3 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, avoid overconfidence in trend continuation — add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or declining.
